summary: ELI currently has 6 registry-defined specialist capability row(s). 3 are recommended for this project now, while 0 remain missing or future-ready rather than being silently assumed available.
eli_authority_note: ELI remains the main interface, synthesizer, and judge. Extensions are optional subordinate instruments whose outputs must still pass through ELI evaluation before they matter.

available_capabilities.label: Coding & Implementation Help
available_capabilities.purpose: Use code and architecture critique to tighten implementation structure, boundaries, and runtime/state design without replacing ELI judgment.
available_capabilities.why_it_would_help: Implementation-package review is live and current blockers still include architecture, firmware, memory, or boundary-sensitive questions.

available_capabilities.label: Visualization & Rendering Help
available_capabilities.purpose: Use visual or layout-oriented drafting support to clarify UI, overlays, diagrams, and implementation-facing visual explanations.
available_capabilities.why_it_would_help: Current review fronts are heavily visual or layout-shaped, so rendering-oriented support could clarify options without replacing ELI judgment.

available_capabilities.label: Embedded Device Integration Help
available_capabilities.purpose: Use embedded-device integration critique for device services, interface mapping, and hardware-adjacent runtime questions when they become materially relevant.
available_capabilities.why_it_would_help: Hardware, wireless, and firmware-adjacent subsystem pressure is now real enough that embedded integration critique could reduce blind spots.

available_capabilities.label: Structured Report & Packaging Help
available_capabilities.purpose: Use structured packaging support to assemble reports, diagrams, or review artifacts without treating formatting as project judgment.
available_capabilities.why_it_would_help: Review drafts and implementation-package review are active, so packaging help could improve clarity later without changing core judgment.

available_capabilities.label: Hardware Implementation Specialist
available_capabilities.purpose: Registry-defined specialist capability available for optional ELI consultation.

available_capabilities.label: Controls & Benchmarking Help
available_capabilities.purpose: Use controls or telemetry-oriented support only when the project has a real control-loop, tuning, or benchmarking question rather than generic build pressure.
available_capabilities.why_not_needed_yet: This project does not currently show a grounded control-loop, actuator, or benchmarking problem that would justify controls help.

representation_risks: Do not present extensions as equal minds; ELI remains the synthesizer, judge, and operator-facing authority.
Do not let registry-backed capability labels imply one-click enablement or hidden autonomous execution when this surface is informational only.
Do not recommend every specialist for every project; extension fit must remain tied to current build, review, and realism pressure.
Missing capability rows are future-ready or high-value gaps, not hidden integrations that already exist.
